records.official_section: Wizards' Vanguard reference says the physical Vanguard supplemental oversized cards alter starting hand size, starting life, and player abilities, and were used in Arena seasons beginning in 1997.
records.source_caveat: Vanguard cards are outside ordinary deck construction and are not a separate tournament-legal premier expansion; PVAN is a later catalog code assigned by Scryfall.

records.official_section: Wizards Japan's 1997 Worlds historical deck retrospective names Jakub Slemr's 5 Color Black list and expressly attributes its printed deck record to 1997 World Championship Decks.
records.source_caveat: This is a later officially published retrospective of one 1997 deck, not a period box announcement or independently printed WC97 code or full packaged print inventory.

records.official_section: Wizards Japan's 1998 Worlds historical Standard-deck feature describes Brian Selden's recurring Nightmare/Survival winning list and identifies the 1998 World Championship Decks product.
records.source_caveat: The official retrospective supports one 1998 deck product name, not a complete 1998 sold-package count or an explicit Wizards WC98 catalog-code declaration.

records.official_section: The official Japanese translation of Wizards' From the Vault: Twenty feature recalls a purchased Kai Budde World Championship Decks 1999 product and notes Wizards made gold-bordered Worlds top-deck products.
records.source_caveat: A product-memory reference is weaker than a contemporary 1999 box description; WC99 is a frozen Scryfall crosswalk rather than an official code visible in this publication.

records.official_section: Wizards Japan's historical Standard article reproduces Tom van de Logt's Parallax Replenish deck and expressly cites the Wizards World Championship Decks 2000 product page as its reference.
records.source_caveat: Its linked original product page now redirects to the generic Wizards archive; the still-readable Japanese retrospective supports the named 2000 product but not a WC00 code.

records.official_section: Wizards Japan's 2004 Worlds historical Eternal Slide Standard article lists champion Julien Nuijten's deck and specifically credits the World Championship Decks 2004 Theme Deck reference.
records.source_caveat: The original legacy Wizards product page has been redirected; an official retrospective deck attribution does not fully reproduce physical 2004 packaging or printings.

records.official_section: Wizards Play Network's June 2020 Love Your Local Game Store launch details Reliquary Tower, Mechagodzilla/Hangarback Walker promos, and reopening-support event kits distributed to WPN stores.
records.source_caveat: A 2020 campaign may contain several promotional printing kinds, not a separate expansion; PLG20 is a frozen Scryfall grouping, not a printed code in this WPN announcement.

records.official_section: Wizards' June 2021 Love Your Local Game Store Summer of Legend announcement details retro-frame Fabled Passage and five more named promos beginning July 23, 2021.
records.source_caveat: This announcement is about the 2021 promotional campaign, not a complete collector-number inventory or any official declaration of the Scryfall PLG21 code.

records.official_section: Wizards' June 2022 Love Your Local Game Store announcement details a foil retro-frame Sol Ring reward for purchasing qualifying sealed Magic products beginning July 1, 2022.
records.source_caveat: This is a local-store promotional print, not a premier set; PLG22 is a Scryfall grouping and the announcement alone does not establish every included card.

records.official_section: The Wizards Play Network June 2024 Love Your Local Game Store article announces its July 5 Draft promotion and a full-art Sakura-Tribe Elder promo for qualifying Modern Horizons 3 activities.
records.source_caveat: The LYLGS 2024 promo program is not an independently sold set, and the WPN article does not print Scryfall's exact PLG24 code or certify all variants.

caveats: Each of these ten source references provides a specifically dated Wizards product-family or event-program account, not an official Scryfall code assertion.
World Championship Decks year references in the official Japanese retrospectives are historically useful but are not restored originals of the sold product pages.
Love Your Local Game Store promotional campaigns are organized separately by year for source review, not treated as new tabletop expansion products.
The 1997 physical Vanguard oversized supplement has different play rules from ordinary collectible Magic deck cards; no mainstream constructed legality is certified.
Yearly event and product-family sources cannot establish exact archival card printing or collector-number inventories, individual first-printing dates, or present-day legality.
